name: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: Free cash flow was negative in Q1 FY25; management expects positive FCF in Q2 and aims to break even or be profitable for the full year.
items.quote: I think for Q2 definitely we will be positive. And it's a little hard to predict what will happen by the end of the year, but our goal is to at least break even in the current year, if not probably in profit.

items.statement: Cash surplus increased to Rs 1245 crore as of 30 June 2024 from Rs 1178 crore as of 31 March 2024
items.quote: The Company has total Cash Surplus of Rs. 1245 crores as on 30th June, 2024 as against Cash Surplus of Rs. 1178 crores as on 31st March, 2024.

items.statement: Management expects credit cost of around INR 45 crores for the full year if NPAs decline, implying ~12 bps credit cost.
items.quote: So we still believe that around INR 45 crores or thereabouts will be the final or roughly thereabouts would be the final provisioning for the entire year, if the NPAs go down.

items.statement: Remediation costs running at INR4 crores per quarter, expected to continue at least one more quarter
items.quote: Typically, our remediation has been about INR4 crores per quarter. And we are maintaining the same run rate.

items.statement: Other expenses expected to stabilize at INR110-120 crores per quarter going forward
items.value: INR110 crores , INR120 crores per quarter
items.quote: I cannot directly quantify everything, but I can roughly tell you that you can expect, I think other expenses in total, we'll be able to maintain in the margin of INR110 crores , INR120 crores per quarter going forward.

items.statement: Carlyle and Advent affiliated funds exercised outstanding warrants boosting CET1 by ~100 basis points
items.quote: I am pleased to also report the exercise of outstanding warrants by CA Basque and Verventa Holdings, which are the funds affiliated and managed by Carlyle and Advent International, which boosted the Bank's CET1 by ~100 basis points.

items.statement: Rights issue was oversubscribed and completed
items.quote: We also thank our shareholders for an overwhelming support and subscription to our rights issue, which is oversubscribed.

items.statement: Free cash flow generation will exceed guided EBITDA
items.quote: We have used up significant opening inventories to improve our free cash generation, which will result in an improved cash flow greater than our guided EBITDA.

items.statement: Free cash generation expected to exceed guidance by about INR100 crores
items.quote: Our free cash generation, like I said, it will be greater than our guidance by at least about INR100 crores.

items.statement: Promoter holding increased to 83%+ after open offer; one year to reduce to 75% minimum public shareholding via block deals or offer for sale.
items.quote: pursuant to the open offer, the promoter's shareholding actually increased to 83+% and we have a stipulated timeframe of one year to bring it back to the minimum public shareholding of 75%.

items.statement: Promoters will sell shares to reduce holding; open to institutional, retail, or HNI investors.
items.quote: No, so promoter will be selling, and it will largely be open to the investors , it could be Institutional, Retail or HNI.

items.statement: Minority shareholders approved related party transactions with Proximus Group; some synergies may take time to ramp up.
items.quote: We are thankful to all our minority shareholders for approving the related party transactions. Some of these related party transactions may take time to ramp up.

items.statement: One-time cost of Rs. 8.6 million incurred for expert opinions on transfer pricing for related-party transactions with Proximus Group and mandatory tender offer.
items.quote: one-time cost of Rs. 8.6 million incurred for seeking expert opinions on transfer pricing for the related-party transactions with the Proximus Group and for the mandatory tender offer.

items.statement: Normalized cash flow conversion from EBITDA stood at 110% in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: The normalized cash flow conversion from EBITDA stood at 110%, you may refer to Slide 17 of the earnings presentation.

items.statement: Free cash generation expected to improve meaningfully in FY25; cash conversion from EBITDA targeted at 50% to 75% band.
items.quote: The free cash generation for the business should improve meaningfully during the year and we expect the cash conversion from EBITDA to be within the 50% to 75% band.

items.statement: Advance to telco supplier of Rs. 38.8 million treated as refundable security deposit under IndAS 109; expected to be consumed by November-December.
items.quote: This is for the security deposit that we have given for our firewall deal, and that security deposit essentially is being treated under IndAS 109 accounting standards, and hence there is a non -cash charge to the purchase account.

items.statement: Short-term loan advance to telco will get consumed by November-December of this calendar year.
items.quote: which we have called out in the cash flow, which is an advance to the telco, which will get consumed by November - December of this financial year, of this calendar year, rather.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance excluding receivables is 141 crores as of end of June
items.quote: Minus receivables. 141. crores.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved to 129 days in Q1 FY25 from 159 days in Q1 FY24
items.quote: The Cash Conversion Cycle for Q1 FY25 stood at 129 days as compared to 159 days in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Net operating cash flow expected to be above 60% of EBITDA as growth stabilizes at 30-35%
items.quote: As we stabilize our growth to what we are saying is 30 %, 35%, you will start seeing the cash conversion cycle significantly improving. And we believe that we will be above 60 % of our EBITDA, the net operating cash.

items.statement: Free cash flow from operations negative in Q1 FY25 but better than Q1 FY24; targeting 30% of EBITDA for full year
items.quote: If you will see, this Q1 is our softest quarter of all the quarters which are there. So, in this quarter, our cash flows, net cash, free cash flows from operations are always negative, though they are still better from what we had in the last quarter. Last Q1, financial year 24. But going forward, you will see we are targeting around at least 30% of our free cash flows to EBITDA.

items.statement: Company raised Rs. 500 crores through a qualified institutional placement (QIP) completed in 3 weeks.
items.quote: We are delighted to announce the significant achievement for our organization as they successfully raised Rs. 500 crores through a qualified institutional placement in just 3 weeks' time, marking a historic milestone in the Indian market.

items.statement: ESOPs granted by parent company API Holdings to Thyrocare employees; no cash impact or share dilution at Thyrocare level
items.quote: These are ESOPs granted from the parent. So these are actually API ESOPs that are granted to Thyrocare employees and recorded in the P&L. So there is actually no cash impact and no share dilution at a Thyrocare level.

items.statement: First quarter cash generation close to INR 40 crores; annual cash generation INR 150-175 crores
items.quote: Even in the first quarter, our cash generation will be, I think, close to INR 40 crores. So we generate INR150 crores, INR175 crores in that range of cash every year.

items.statement: Free cash flow generation and operating efficiency drive healthy net cash position; cash equivalent balance close to INR 9,000 crores as of 30 June 2024
items.quote: Our free cash flow generation and operating efficiency continues to drive healthy net cash position. As at 30th June 2024, debt on our balance sheet is INR547 crores constituting lease liability as well as working capital. Cash equivalent balance is touching close to about INR9,000 crores.

items.statement: Board approved acquisition of Patanjali Ayurved's Home & Personal Care business on slump sale basis for INR1,100 crores, awaiting CCI and shareholder approval
items.quote: The Board approved the valuation of the acquisition during the quarter and later on 1st of July 2024, it approved the acquisition of PAL's Home & Personal Care business on a slump sale basis at a cost of INR1,100 crores.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents increased by $19.2 million to $280.9 million; DSOs improved by 1 day to 72 days due to healthy collections
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents increased further by $19.2 million to $280.9 million, and DSOs improved by 1 day to 72 days on account of healthy collection contributing to overall financial health and operational agility of the company.

items.statement: Chairman Sharad Upasani retired as Independent Director on 22 July 2024 after completing second term; Prakash Apte appointed Non-Executive Chairman from 23 July 2024; Dr. Vandana Agarwal appointed Independent Director from 23 July 2024
items.quote: Mr. Sharad Upasani, Chairman, retired as an Independent Director with close of business hours on 22 July 2024 on account of completion of his second term of the office as an Independent Director as per the provisions of law and consequently ceased to be the Chairman of the Board. Mr. Prakash Apte, Independent Director, has been appointed as Non-Executive Chairman of the Board with effect from July

items.statement: Completed share buyback for non-promoter shareholders amounting to Rs.46.62 crores inclusive of all taxes
items.quote: As you all know the Company has recently completed a share buyback for non-promoter shareholders, amounting to Rs.46.62 crores inclusive of all taxes.

items.statement: Incremental cost of borrowing remained in the 7.8% to 8% corridor for Q1 FY25.
items.quote: We don't want to be so specific, but it has remained in the same corridor of 7.8% to 8%.

items.statement: Cash balance is around INR 650-plus crores
items.quote: And the cash balance now is in the range of around INR650-plus crores.

items.statement: Another call of INR 30 on partly paid shares planned for Q4 FY25, 6-9 months away, company does not need capital now
items.quote: There will be another call of INR 30 that we are planning to do in the Q4 of FY of this year. So probably next 6 months to 9 months based on the current requirement.

items.statement: Trade receivables grew from INR 1,458 crores to INR 2,052 crores due to higher shipments; collected about INR 1,170 crores during the quarter
items.quote: Trade receivables grew from INR1,458 crores to INR2,052 crores. This again is increased due to higher shipments in Q1 but we made progress in terms of collections as well and we collected about INR1,170 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: ESOP program launched for key people; Q2 FY25 will have full quarter ESOP impact of 1% on margins vs 0.7% in Q1
items.quote: Last quarter, it was 0.7%, this quarter (Q2FY25) would be 1%. So , this coming quarter will be 1%, last quarter was 0.7%.

items.statement: First quarter recovery run rate is Rs 35 crore; expects similar or better run rate for remaining three quarters.
items.quote: So our first quarter run rate recovery is about Rs. 35 crore, right? We would expect that run rate to hold up for this year.

items.statement: Receivables are managed through a cash-and-carry model with advances from distributors; inventory holding is 40-45 days on average.
items.quote: In terms of receivable etc., we deal in cash and carry business where mostly the advances come fro m distributors and then we do the billing to our dealers etc

items.statement: Management confirmed they are working on a QIP to raise funds for inorganic growth and international expansion.
items.quote: we have already declared, and we are already working around the QIP so that we have much larger stake in payment ecosystem and at the same time, we have first mover advantage in several solutions

items.statement: Free cash flow was negative in Q2 CY24 due to capex capitalization in Q1 and Q2, but improved versus Q1; working capital rose to 20.2% of sales and is a focus area.
items.quote: We did have some challenges on the free cash flow, particularly coming on the back of the capex investments, which got capitalized in the quarter. The first quarter and the second quarter put together, got capitalized and hence, we see a negative ca sh flow

items.statement: Inventories rose 0.6 percentage points of sales versus last year due to higher projected business and 20-25 day longer transit times from logistics issues; receivables increased after payment-term adjustments aligned with market conditions.
items.quote: Yes, inventories are slightly higher as a percentage to sales. If we see the quarterly trends of past year usually in June, there is increase. And this time increase is even slightly higher, 0.6% point of sales, it is higher than last year.

items.statement: Operating cash flow was poor in H1 due to high inventory and receivables, but CFO says it is temporary and working capital is comfortable
items.quote: Yes, it's more of a temporary phenomenon because we had a high inventory end of June. And at the same time, we had a higher accounts receivable, so it happens and sometimes go up and down.

items.statement: Company received 25% of warrant amount for technology, general development and margin funding
items.quote: Right now, we have taken this by way of warrant, and we have not received full amount, around 25% amount we have received, and it is for overall technology and general development and with margin funding also.

items.statement: Board approved raising up to 8,500 crore via AT1 and Tier-2 bonds; 4,000 crore AT1 and 4,500 crore Tier-2.
items.quote: But, tier -1 and tier-2 AT1 bonds and tier -2 bonds, the board has already permitted the management to go to the market to the extent of 8,500 crores to raise. Out of that, 4,000 crores is AT1 bonds and 4,500 crores is tier -2 bonds.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs 1,197 crore as of June 2024
items.quote: We are also pleased to report that our balance sheet as of June 2024 demonstrates a further position of strength with a consolidated strong net worth of 4,253 crores and a net cash position of 1,197 crores.

items.statement: Promoter preferential capital infusion expected to close by Q2 FY25 after document submission and clearance
items.quote: Promoter capital, there are a few more documents that have been sou ght for. We are in the process submitting it and once that happens we would get the clearance and once the clearance comes in the capital inflow should happen in a few days, if not weeks

items.statement: Repaid one-fourth of Sunflame acquisition term loan in April (~INR70 cr) and another one-fourth by end of July; aim to repay full loan by end of FY25 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: So in April, we repaid one-fourth of the term loan we had taken. It is about INR70 crores that we have repaid and a similar amount will get repaid by end of this month.

items.statement: Debtor days fell to 35 days in Q1 FY25 due to strong season and timely customer payments; creditor days rose to 75 days due to higher buying volumes in May and June
items.quote: So debtors have come down, they are lower than our normative levels because it was a strong season, so customers pay on time. Otherwise, similarly, even on the payable side, even May and June, both were big months.

items.statement: Mr. Ramachandran retired as Chairman effective June 30, 2024; Mr. Sandeep Batra re-designated as Chairman from same date.
items.quote: We express our sincere gratitude to Mr. Ramachandran, who has retired from the position of Chairman of the Board of Directors effective June 30, 2024. Mr. Sandeep Batra has been re-designated as Chairman with effect from the same date.

items.statement: Mr. Suresh Vaswani appointed as additional Independent Director effective July 4, 2024, subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: I am also pleased to inform you that Mr. Suresh Vaswani has been appointed as an additional Independent Director effective July 4, 2024, subject to the approval of the Shareholders.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents plus unavailed cash credit limit and documented unavailed sanction totaled INR 30.1 billion as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: As of 30th June 2024, we maintained sufficient liquidity in the form of cash and cash equivalents and unavailed cash credit limit of INR17.5 billion and documented unavailed sanction of INR12.6 billion.

items.statement: Management states current debt position at Spencer's standalone is around Rs. 700 crores, Natures Basket about Rs. 100 crores, consolidated about Rs. 800 crores.
items.quote: The current debt position, yes . So, at Spencer's standalone, it is around Rs. 700 crores and at Natures Basket it is at least about Rs. 100 crores, at a consol level, about Rs. 800 crores.

items.statement: CD ratio targeted at 85% inclusive of IBPC securitization to manage liquidity and reduce negative carry
items.quote: To better manage liquidity and to reduce the negative carry, we have targeted maintaining our CD ratio at 85% inclusive of IBPC securitization.

items.statement: Standalone operational cash flow was Rs 61.84 crore in Q1 FY25 due to reduction of advances to creditors, realization from inventory and trade receivables, and other management measures.
items.quote: Standalone operational cash flow of the company is Rs. 61.84 Crores due to reduction of advances to creditors, realization from inventory and trade receivables and other measures taken by the management.

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to raise up to ₹2400 crores via equity or convertible securities for potential acquisitions and strategic opportunities.
items.quote: So, first thing, it's an enabling resolution. It allows us to raise up to ₹2400 crores.

items.statement: Paid first interim dividend of ₹8 per share during Q1 FY25
items.quote: we have paid the first interim dividend of ₹8 per share during the quarter, demonstrating our commitment to maximizing shareholder value.

items.statement: Epavo will be a 50-50 JV with Ram Ratna Wires; EPACK will be a customer for AC motors, creating related-party transactions on arm's length basis.
items.quote: So, this company, Epavo especially for air conditioned motors, yes, EPACK would be one of the customers. So, there will be some related party transactions to that extent, but yes, since this is the Motor Company especially so we are open to self, we will be catering to almost all the customers.

items.statement: EPACK targets sourcing 40-50% of its motor purchases from Epavo in FY25.
items.quote: I think we would be targeting anywhere between 40% and 50% of EPACK's motor buying from Epavo, let us put it this way.

items.statement: Telangana receivables stretched from 60 days to over 150 days in FY24, causing working capital stress and flat volume growth.
items.quote: Last year for us, in terms of overall volume was flat for the reasons that we have already sort of covered in our some of our previous calls, which is largely due to non-availability of working capital largely on account of Telangana, which is a large market where receivables went from 60 days to over 150 days

items.statement: Telangana receivables situation improved but not fully resolved; industry overdue around Rs 4,000 crores, company operating north of 100 days vs agreed 45-60 days.
items.quote: The situation is better than earlier. But the full issue is yet to be resolved. The industry, the beer and the spirits industry through its industry body, CIABC, and the new beer industry body, they simply had a meeting with both the current government and the bureaucrats and we have presented our case to them and they have given us an assurance that they will resolve the issue starting September.

items.statement: Interest cost expected to cut more than half in FY25 due to debt repayment post-IPO, with legacy interest cost in Q1.
items.quote: we are e xpecting interest cost to cut more than half in this financial year, largely because Q1 we have legacy interest cost , so that’s what we are projecting for FY25 and then progressively reduce it out

items.statement: Chairman stepped down from executive to non-executive role from 1 July 2023, creating separation between management and ownership.
items.quote: The chairman has from 1 st of July, 2023 stepped down from being an executive chairman to a non-executive chairman, which actually helps in terms of creating a separation between the management and the ownership

items.statement: Board strengthened with several independent directors; digitizing board practice and moving compliances to SaaS platform.
items.quote: Strengthening of the board with several independent director s brings in the right management practices. The focus in terms of the owners and compliances ever increasing. We are also looking at digitizing our entire risk practice. We have already digitized our board practice and we are also looking at the compliances to get on t o a SaaS platform

items.statement: Chairman's office cost of Rs 93-95 crores saved from FY25 after stepping down from executive role on 1 July 2023.
items.quote: The cost that you’re referring to in the R HP was the cost associated with the chairman who has stepped down from being an executive chairman to a non-executive chairman w.e.f. 1st July ‘23. So, the 90-odd crores is the total cost that was associated. Part of that cost was incurred in Q1 FY24 and that cost since then we are not incurring. Therefore , we get a full benefit in FY25 moving forward

items.statement: IPO completed; debt issues resolved post-listing, balance sheet deleveraged.
items.quote: On back of post-IPO, we paid off our debts, it's a de leverage balance sheet, we do not have any further working capital stress.

items.statement: Overall debt reduced by approximately Rs 82 crore from Q4 FY24 to Q1 FY25, from Rs 1,047 crore to Rs 965 crore.
items.quote: For current quarter, overall debt stands at Rs.965 CR versus 1,047 CR in Q4 FY24, thus a reduction of approximate 82 CR.

items.statement: Operating cash flow was $53 million, representing 110% of net income for the quarter.
items.quote: Cash flow generation at $53 million for the quarter was 110% of net income.

items.statement: Board approved raising up to INR 1,000 crores through QIP; 25-30% may be used for inorganic opportunities, majority for capex
items.quote: The Board recently g ave approval to raise up to INR 1,000 crores through QIP process which was done through a board meeting end of June

items.statement: Net operating cash flow was Rs. 287 crores in Q1 FY25, supported by strong collections and IC business revenue.
items.quote: The net operating cash flow which is excluding the land related outflows, and all was about Rs. 287 crores. This was supported by strong collections during the quarter as well as the IC business which generated good amount of revenue.

items.statement: Operating cash flow before land outflows has averaged Rs. 650 crores annually from FY22 onwards; Q1 FY25 was Rs. 287 crores with target to equal or exceed last year.
items.quote: Cash flow from operations which is before payments towards land outgo, if we look at last couple of years from FY22 onwards , it's been in the upwards of Rs. (+600) crores. In fact, Rs. 650 crores would probably be the average. Even for the 1st Quarter we are at Rs. 287 crores and the target is to be equal to or more than what we have clocked in the last year.

items.statement: Free cash flow grew 118% year-on-year in Q1 FY25; residential collections jumped 96% to Rs. 540 crores.
items.quote: Compared to the last year same quarter it's about 118% growth over the prior year and the residential collections for us you know which stood at Rs. 540 crores for this quarter is also close to a 96% jump over the prior year.

items.statement: Discussions underway for fundraise at Mahindra Group level, with external fund houses and global partners; details to be shared when concluded.
items.quote: There are I would say three four discussion that is going on, given they are internally at Mahindra level, externally with some of the other fund houses as well as some of the global partners who have interest in pursuing India opportunity and India real estate opportunity with a credible responsible player.

items.statement: Management confirmed five long-term capacity holders owe use-or-pay dues and that bank guarantees of Rs 378 crore for CY2021 and Rs 798 crore for CY2022 have been received.
items.quote: First of all, I would like to clarify here that this settlement mechanism was approved by the board for calendar year 2021 and 2022 and we have received the bank guarantees to the extent of Rs. 378 crores for 2021 and Rs. 798 crores for the calendar year 2022.

items.statement: Management said the 7.5 MTPA Qatar contract renewal and back-to-back offtake agreements are still under discussion and will require annual shareholder approval as a material related-party transaction.
items.quote: We are still in discussion. But as and when there is final agreement with them, we will let you know. But these things are going on, but they have already committed to that because when we signed, they have assured us that they will take it.

items.statement: Management stated Q1 FY25 capex was around Rs 300 crore and full-year FY25 capex target is around Rs 3,500 crore.
items.quote: Q1 CAPEX is around Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Management stated Q1 FY25 capex was around Rs 300 crore and full-year FY25 capex target is around Rs 3,500 crore.
items.quote: This year, CAPEX target is around Rs. 3,500 crores.

items.statement: Management said Rs 63 crore of use-or-pay revenue booked in 2021-22 was reversed in Q1 FY25 after a customer supplied makeup volumes, and the waiver relates to both 2021 and 2022.
items.quote: Rs. 63 crores has been reversed because we have got the equivalent volume from the concerned customer, and we have earned more than that.

items.statement: Management confirmed provisions for use-or-pay dues will continue until payments are realized, and that the Rs 129 crore provision in Q1 FY25 is based on the standard formula.
items.quote: Provisions will be done, it's an accounting aspect. We will continue to make the provision because payment until it is realized provision will continue.

items.statement: Cash balance is minimal at INR 20-25 crores; company prefers unutilized bank lines over holding cash
items.quote: So, we do not carry any cash balance, maybe INR 20 Crores to INR 25 Crores kind of thing in the collection, otherwise, right now, we don't have a cash balance.

items.statement: Management concluded a successful QIP attracting prominent global and Indian institutions.
items.quote: Q1 was quite eventful for us from a strategic perspective as well, we concluded a succe ssful QIP and it's very encouraging to attract prominent global and Indian institutions to join us in this mission to create a global tech player rooted in

name: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India Ltd

items.statement: Cash balance improved to Rs 1,437 crore with 7.73% yield
items.quote: Our cash position also improved to Rs. 1,437 crore and as of now we are generating a yield of about 7.73% per annum.

items.statement: Completed QIP raising INR 800 crores with INR 2,800 crores demand
items.quote: We are pleased to announce the successful completion of our qualified institution placement, raising INR 800 crores. The QIP received an overwhelming response with total demand reaching approximately INR 2,800 crores reflecting strong institutional confidence.

items.statement: Warrants issued in December 2023 with 18-month subscription period; 25-26% subscribed so far, remaining expected over next 12 months adding ~Rs. 44 crores to net worth
items.quote: warrants basically were issued in December 2023. And the warrants typically has a period of 18 months for the subscription. So just to let you know, around 25% to 26% of the amount has been subscribed, remaining is expected to get subscribed over the next 12 months

items.statement: Management exploring additional capital raise from HNIs and family offices beyond warrant subscription, subject to board approval
items.quote: we are getting interest from HNI from f amily offices to basically be a participant in the long term growth plan of the company. And depending on the calibration as to how we want to basically scale up that particular action will be basically obviously presented to the Board and Board will take a call on whether to raise more capital so in addition to the warrant side of it

items.statement: Board approved 1:10 stock split subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: The Board has also considered and approved a sub-division/split of 1 Equity Share having face value of INR10 each into 10 equity shares having face value of INR1 each by alteration of capital clause in the Memorandum of Association of the company, subject to approval of the members of the company in the ensuing General Meeting.

items.statement: Cash logistics business achieved highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR171 crores with 17% EBITDA margin and PAT of INR14 crores
items.quote: We're very happy to report that the business has achieved its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR171 crores, which translates to an impressive growth of 12% on a Y-o-Y basis. The Cash business expanded its EBITDA by 130 basis points, at a 17% EBITDA margin, and a PAT of INR14 crores translating to 32% Y-o-Y growth and a PAT margin of 8.1% in this quarter.

items.statement: DAM Capital appointed to run demerger process for cash management business, documentation nearly ready
items.quote: Well, DAM Capital has just been appointed to run the process and documentation is more or less ready. Hopefully, in the next quarter, we'll have good clarity around that.

items.statement: Company raised INR500 crores equity through QIP in Q1 FY25, first equity raise since 2017 IPO
items.quote: As you all know, during the quarter, the company raised INR500 crores equity through QIP . This QIP marked the first equity raised by company since its IPO in 2017.

items.statement: Company maintained average cash and cash equivalents of around INR800 crores excluding QIP proceeds and unutilized cash credit facilities of around INR600 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: company through its efficient liability management was able to maintain an average cash and cash equivalent of around INR800 crores excluding the QIP proceeds of INR500 crores and unutilized cash credit facilities of around INR600 crores.

items.statement: CGFMU audit nearing closure with positive outcome expected
items.quote: The audit process is nearing a closure. The management is confident of having a positive closure soon.

items.statement: CEO succession process on track with search firm appointed
items.quote: As informed earlier, the board has appointed a search firm to assist in identifying potential candidates to take on the role of MD & CEO. Due process is being followed by the board in this regard, and the same is on track.

items.statement: QIP proceeds of INR 650 Crore used for debt reduction, INR 250 Crore for DR Axion acquisition, INR 300 Crore for general corporate purposes
items.quote: One is INR 250 Crore was for the acquisition of DR Axion and it is very clear in the stated proceeds. And 25% was for general corporate, which is around INR 300 Crore. So, only INR 650 Crore was going to debt reduction.

items.statement: DR Axion acquisition completed 17 months ago, no new CAPEX needed, cash flow excellent, management intact with eight Korean expatriates continuing
items.quote: DR Axion is now practically 17 months; it has been completed. I think it is not a capital intensive. We are not looking at CAPEX there. It is only maintenance CAPEX and a very marginal CAPEX. The cash flow is excellent, and the management is intact.

items.statement: MoU signed for Sunbeam acquisition, due diligence near completion, no debt takeover, Gurgaon plant largely excluded due to labor issues, export business partially transferred
items.quote: we are not taking over any debt of the company. That is clear on this matter. So, that is 100% very clear from day one on this matter. So, whatever is the finalization, which is going to happen, it will be for the business and assets somewhat on the t heme of Fronberg, but whether we are taking over the assets or whether we are taking over the company, only time will tell

items.statement: CAPEX for FY25 stands at INR 201 Crore for two greenfield plants at Kothavadi and Bhiwadi, Phase-1 trial production expected in Q4 FY25
items.quote: CAPEX for FY '25 stands at INR 201 Crore. We are putting up two plants, one in Kothavadi and one in Bhiwadi. And I will make a separate note of that at the end of this statement.

items.statement: QIP successfully raised, proceeds allocated to DR Axion acquisition, debt reduction, and general corporate purposes
items.quote: I wish to reiterate that we are subscale in the Powertrain as well as aluminum division and when we look at the growth opportunities for the global requirement, we need to change our mindset from small scale to at least medium scale, I would say, in the global context. So, this is what the

name: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Ltd

items.statement: Promoter pledged shares to be released between August and December
items.quote: Yes. So we are looking to clear the pledge between the window of August and December. So most of the pledge should get released between this window.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS operating cash flow of INR32 crores in June 2024
items.quote: We achieved a strong pre-Ind AS operating cash flow of INR32 crores in June '24.

items.statement: Management does not provide Q1 bad debt data; reconciled at year-end.
items.quote: I don't think we have any data on Q1 basis. These are numbers that are reconciled end of the year.

items.statement: Company initiated equity fundraise of INR2,000 million (INR200 crores) through preferential allotment to drive sustainable growth.

items.quote: Net working capital at the end of the June quarter was at about 121 days, which is similar to the previous year's same quarter.

items.statement: Net debt adjusted for unutilized proceeds at INR5,771 million end of Q1 FY25 versus INR972 million end of June quarter FY24
